_comment: add agent（atommem 逐 message 抽取）的统一配置：agent 能看到的一切（工具描述、命令行用法、
目录布局、响应协议、原子标准、system prompt）都在这里，单一事实源。
src/codemem/search/toolcfg.py 渲染注入；src/codemem/search/tools.py 执行语义。
结构与 configs/tool.json 完全一致（复用同一套 ToolCatalog），只是 prompt/策略不同。
与 search 的关键差别：agent 不再产出 evidence，而是把**原子事实**追加进 atommem.jsonl；
它只填 memory + metadata.{time, role, tag} 四个字段，id/source/type/changelog 由系统补。
system prompt 的正文在 src/codemem/prompts.py 的 ATOM_AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT（这里只放槽位壳）。

protocol.response_format: Reply with exactly ONE JSON object per turn, nothing else -- no prose, no markdown fence.
protocol.done_signal: When you have written the target message's atoms into atommem.jsonl, reply with plain text (not JSON). That is how you finish. If the target yields no atom, finish immediately.
protocol.quote_arg_safety: Always wrap command strings in double quotes in the JSON; escape inner double quotes as \".

read.description: Read a file, or a slice of one (`offset`/`limit` are 1-based line numbers). Truncated to 2000 lines / 50KB. Use it to read earlier messages (msgmem.jsonl) or the session summaries (summem.jsonl).
guidelines: `grep -n` first to find the line number, then `read` with offset/limit around it.

path.description: Path to the file to read

edit.description: The ONLY way to write files. Two modes -- pass exactly one. APPEND (`append="<text>"`) adds text to the end (creating the file if missing) -- use it for a NEW atom. REPLACE (`edits=[{"oldText","newText"}]`) rewrites text that already exists -- use it to MERGE: when a fact is already in atommem.jsonl and the target message confirms/extends it, rewrite that existing atom into ONE atom (keep its id and source, add this message's id to `source`) instead of appending a near-duplicate.
guidelines: New atom -> APPEND (path defaults to atommem.jsonl): {"tool":"edit","args":{"append":"<one JSON atom>\n"}}
Existing fact -> REPLACE: copy the exact line, rewrite `memory`/`time` as needed, keep `metadata.id`, and put ALL supporting ids in `metadata.source` -- e.g. source ["session_3_16","session_8_16"].
Merge one fact into ONE atom. Never leave two atoms that say the same thing in different words.
Never pass both `append` and `edits` in one call.
There is NO `write` tool: you cannot overwrite the whole file, so you can never erase earlier atoms by accident.

path.description: Path to edit. Defaults to atommem.jsonl if omitted.

append.description: Text to add to the end of the file (created if missing). Use this for new atoms.

edits.description: Exact replacements. Use only to fix an existing atom.

bash.description: Run a bash command in the working directory. stdout+stderr combined; truncated to the last 2000 lines / 50KB. `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `head`, `wc`, `sort`, `uniq` are all available -- this is your retrieval toolbox.

description.description: Short present-participle summary, e.g. 'Grepping earlier messages'

grep.summary: Your search tool. One JSON object per line, so `-n` gives you line numbers you can hand to `read`.

recipes.why: Find a name or a word across all three memory files at once (recursive).
Find every atom already written about an entity (cross-session hop). Because references are resolved, the same name means the same thing everywhere.
See what happened in a specific session (its raw messages).
See which session a topic came up in (the summaries).
Read one memory file in full.

time.summary: Compute a date in bash when you need one (`date -d`). Do NOT do the arithmetic in your head -- you will get it wrong. Anchor on the message's own session time. The environment is pinned to LC_ALL=C so month and weekday names always come out in English.

recipes.why: Relative -> absolute. The raw form ('1:56 pm on 8 May, 2023') is accepted as-is.
Which weekday a date is -- needed when the source says 'the Friday before X'.

layout: msgmem.jsonl    -- every raw message, one per line (id = session_N_M, type 'msg'). Wording is raw; each line carries its session time. Use it to resolve who/what a pronoun refers to.
summem.jsonl    -- one summary per session (id = session_N_summary, type 'summary'). Use it to see which session a topic came up in.
atommem.jsonl   -- the atoms produced so far (id = session_N_M_K, type 'atom'). THIS IS YOUR OUTPUT -- append to it.
rules: Never write msgmem.jsonl or summem.jsonl -- they are read-only; your writes there are rejected.
All files are JSONL: one record per line, so grep works on them directly and line numbers are stable.
Use `grep -rin "word" .` to search all three files at once (recursive).
Only atommem.jsonl is yours to append. Write the TARGET message's atoms there.

strategy:
Your goal: for the ONE target message, make its atomic facts present in atommem.jsonl as self-contained atoms -- each a fact a reader can understand alone, and each fact appearing EXACTLY ONCE.

Write a fact only after you have resolved its references and TIME, and after you have checked it is not already there:

- Resolve references: `grep -rin "<a word from the target>" .` across all three files; `read msgmem.jsonl` for the raw earlier messages; `read summem.jsonl` for the per-session summaries.
- Put ALL the time into `time` (see the TIME standard): a point is an ISO date; a duration / "N ago" / age becomes its START or a SPAN ("married 5 years" on 9 June 2023 -> `2018`); if you cannot compute it, keep the anchored phrase ("5 years before 9 June 2023").
- CHECK BEFORE YOU WRITE: `grep -rin "<the fact's key word>" atommem.jsonl`. If the fact is already there, do NOT append a reworded copy -- REWRITE that atom with `edit` replace so it stays ONE atom, and add this message's id to its `source`. Only APPEND when the fact is new.

Do not guess an entity you could have looked up -- but do not read forever either: a fact needing three searches is worth three; a greeting is worth zero.

prompt.user_begin: Extract the atomic facts of the target message into atommem.jsonl.
prompt.user_no_progress: Several turns have passed without atommem.jsonl changing. If the target message yields no atom, reply with plain text (no JSON) now. Otherwise write the atom.
prompt.user_steps_exhausted: You have used your last turn. Reply with plain text (no JSON) now.
